meta.name: PhysAlts STEM Atlas — Biology, Genomics & Neuroscience Hubs
meta.description: 31 verified global flagship institutes for genomics, molecular biology, structural cryo-EM, CRISPR genome engineering, AI drug discovery, and systems neuroscience.

hubs.name: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
hubs.summary: Unites MIT, Harvard, and Boston teaching hospitals to drive genomic medicine—pioneering eukaryotic CRISPR-Cas9, base and prime editing (David Liu), gnomAD human variation catalogs, and the Human Cell Atlas.
hubs.nobel: Breakthroughs in CRISPR genome engineering (Feng Zhang, David Liu), single-cell RNA-seq, and open GATK genomic software used worldwide.

stages.undergrad: Broad Summer Research Program (BSRP) — 9-week paid genomics and computational biology fellowship.

stages.postdoc: Broad Fellows and Schmidt Center Postdoctoral Fellowships at the ML-biology frontier.
stages.assoc_prof: Core Institute Member and Associate Member collaborative multi-lab initiatives.
stages.prof: Institute Member chairs leading global consortia like the Human Cell Atlas and gnomAD.

rabbitLinks.reason: Steps away in Kendall Square; joint Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center merges machine learning with single-cell biology.

hubs.name: Wellcome Sanger Institute
hubs.summary: Named after two-time Nobel laureate Frederick Sanger, the single largest UK contributor to the Human Genome Project (sequencing one-third of the genome) and now driving the Darwin Tree of Life and Cancer Dependency Map.
hubs.nobel: Founding Director John Sulston won the 2002 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine and championed open-access human genome data.

stages.highschool: Explore yourgenome.org—open interactive genomics guides built by the Wellcome Genome Campus.
stages.undergrad: Sanger Summer Placement internships in bioinformatics, cellular genetics, and pathogen surveillance.

stages.phd: Fully funded 4-year Sanger PhD Programme with University of Cambridge degree award.
stages.postdoc: Sanger Postdoctoral Fellowships in somatic mutation physics, spatial genomics, and Earth BioGenome.
stages.assoc_prof: Group Leader appointments with substantial core Wellcome Trust sequencing budgets.
stages.prof: Head of Programme leadership steering global biodiversity and cancer genomics.

rabbitLinks.reason: Shares the Wellcome Genome Campus in Hinxton—turning massive raw DNA sequencing into global open databases.

hubs.name: EMBL (European Molecular Biology Laboratory)
hubs.summary: Europe's CERN for the life sciences—an intergovernmental treaty lab of 29 member states spanning 6 sites (Heidelberg, Hinxton, Grenoble, Hamburg, Rome, Barcelona) advancing cryo-EM, planetary biology, and structural genomics.
hubs.nobel: Nobel Prizes to Christiane Nüsslein-Volhard & Eric Wieschaus (1995) and Jacques Dubochet (2017, cryo-electron microscopy vitrification developed at EMBL).

stages.highschool: Join EMBL Science Education and Public Engagement (SEPE) virtual lab tours and DNA kits.
stages.undergrad: Paid summer undergraduate research internships across EMBL's 6 European sites.
stages.masters: MSc thesis placements in structural imaging, developmental biology, and bioinformatics.
stages.phd: EMBL International PhD Programme (EIPP) — one of Europe's most sought-after interdisciplinary life-science PhDs.
stages.postdoc: EIPOD-LinC Postdoctoral Fellowships linking two EMBL groups or external physics/AI partners.
stages.assoc_prof: EMBL Group Leader model (9-year max tenure) continuously refreshing Europe's academic leadership.

hubs.summary: The world's largest open molecular data repository—stewarding Ensembl, UniProt, PDBe, ChEMBL, and co-hosting the 200M+ structure AlphaFold Protein Structure Database with Google DeepMind.
hubs.nobel: Critical digital infrastructure enabling modern genomics, proteomics, and Nobel-winning AI structural biology.

hubs.summary: Europe's largest biomedical research institute under a single roof—housing 1,500+ scientists in London's Knowledge Quarter across cancer evolution, virology, immunology, and neural circuits.

hubs.name: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB)
hubs.summary: Arguably the most successful 'Nobel Prize factory' in biological history—originating at Cambridge's Cavendish Physics Lab and birthing X-ray protein structures, DNA sequencing, monoclonal antibodies, C. elegans genetics, and cryo-EM.
hubs.nobel: 12 Nobel Prizes awarded to 16 LMB scientists (Perutz, Kendrew, Crick, Watson, Sanger ×2, Milstein, Köhler, Brenner, Sulston, Ramakrishnan, Henderson, Winter).

hubs.summary: ETH Zurich's dedicated bioengineering and systems-biology department located in Basel's life-science capital—uniting synthetic gene circuits, microfluidics, organoids, and computational immunology.
hubs.nobel: Europe's leading fusion of engineering rigor, single-cell evolutionary genomics, and synthetic cell-therapy design.

stages.highschool: Explore ETH D-BSSE public bioengineering exhibitions in Basel's BSS building.
stages.undergrad: Bachelor projects and iGEM synthetic biology teams competing internationally.
stages.masters: ETH MSc in Biotechnology or Computational Biology & Bioinformatics (English-taught).

stages.assoc_prof: Tenure-track faculty collaborating with University of Basel, FMI, Roche, and Novartis.
stages.prof: Leadership in European organoid bioengineering and quantitative evolutionary epidemiology.

rabbitLinks.reason: Neighbors in Basel—uniting ETH's synthetic bioengineering with FMI's epigenetics and neurobiology.
Extends ETH Zurich's physics and engineering precision directly into living biological systems.

hubs.name: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research (FMI)
hubs.summary: Named after Friedrich Miescher—who isolated DNA ('nuclein') in Basel in 1869—renowned for pioneering discoveries in genome regulation, epigenetics, multicellular organization, and neural circuits.
hubs.nobel: World leader in chromatin architecture, predictive-coding visual neurobiology, and non-coding RNA regulation.

stages.highschool: Learn how Friedrich Miescher first extracted DNA from white blood cells in 1869.
stages.undergrad: Summer research internships in Basel across neurobiology and quantitative cell biology.
stages.masters: MSc theses affiliated with the University of Basel Biozentrum.
stages.phd: FMI International PhD Program (fully funded, cohort-based doctoral training).
stages.postdoc: FMI Postdoctoral Fellowships with state-of-the-art imaging, proteomics, and sequencing cores.
stages.assoc_prof: Junior Group Leader tracks with strong internal funding and Basel academic chairs.
stages.prof: Senior Group Leaders shaping European epigenetics and systems neuroscience.

rabbitLinks.reason: Co-anchors Basel's life sciences campus across the Rhine alongside University of Basel.
Collaborates closely on neural circuit dynamics and predictive-processing models of perception.

projects.name: Genome Regulation & Predictive Neural Circuit Dynamics

hubs.name: Champalimaud Centre for the Unknown
hubs.summary: Striking waterfront research and clinical center where the Tagus River meets the Atlantic—a global hotspot for systems neuroscience, open hardware/AI behavioral tracking (Bonsai), and translational oncology.
hubs.nobel: Awards the €1M António Champalimaud Vision Award and anchors the International Brain Laboratory (IBL) collaboration.

stages.highschool: Attend Champalimaud public science cafés and Lisbon brain-awareness exhibitions.
stages.undergrad: Summer research internships in neuroscience, AI behavior tracking, and cancer biology.
stages.masters: MSc placements in computational neuroscience and biomedical engineering.
stages.phd: International Neuroscience & Cancer Doctoral Programme (INDP) — fully funded 4-year rotations.
stages.postdoc: Postdoctoral fellowships bridging theoretical neuroscience, RL, and physiology.
stages.assoc_prof: Principal Investigator positions with dedicated open-hardware engineering cores.
stages.prof: Leadership across the International Brain Laboratory and digital therapeutics.

rabbitLinks.reason: Systems neuroscientists here study dopamine, timing, and reinforcement learning directly linked to AI theory.

hubs.name: Institut Curie
hubs.summary: Founded by Marie Skłodowska-Curie on rue d'Ulm—uniting a world-class basic research center in cell biophysics, epigenetics, and immunology with one of Europe's leading proton-therapy cancer hospitals.
hubs.nobel: 5 Nobel Prizes across its founders and directors: Marie Curie (×2), Pierre Curie, Irène & Frédéric Joliot-Curie, and Pierre-Gilles de Gennes.

stages.highschool: Visit the free Musée Curie in Marie Curie's historic office and chemistry laboratory.
stages.undergrad: Summer internships in cell mechanics, radiation physics, and cancer genomics.
stages.masters: PSL / Sorbonne M2 thesis placements bridging soft-matter physics with cell biology.
stages.phd: IC-3i International PhD Program (Marie Skłodowska-Curie co-funded interdisciplinary PhDs).
stages.postdoc: Postdoctoral fellowships in active-matter cell biophysics, proton therapy, and chromatin biology.
stages.assoc_prof: ATIP-Avenir Junior Group Leader fellowships launching independent labs in Paris.

rabbitLinks.reason: Literally next door on rue d'Ulm; together they form Paris's Montagne Sainte-Geneviève science hill.

hubs.name: VIB (Flanders Institute for Biotechnology)
hubs.summary: Virtual-yet-tightly-integrated life sciences powerhouse spanning Ghent, Leuven, Brussels, and Antwerp—world leader in plant biotechnology (Marc Van Montagu legacy), single-domain nanobodies, spatial multi-omics, and neurodegeneration.
hubs.nobel: Built on Belgium's pioneering Agrobacterium plant genetics (World Food Prize) and camelid nanobody discovery.

stages.highschool: Explore VIB's open Biotech Stories covering CRISPR agriculture and nanobody medicine.
stages.undergrad: Bachelor and summer placements at VIB-UGent, VIB-KU Leuven, and VIB-VUB centers.
stages.masters: MSc theses in bioinformatics, AI genomics, and structural nanobody engineering.
stages.phd: VIB International PhD Program with competitive Belgian FWO fellowships.
stages.postdoc: VIB.AI Center for AI & Computational Biology postdoctoral tracks.
stages.assoc_prof: Group Leader positions with dedicated tech-transfer and spin-out support.

rabbitLinks.reason: Shares Belgium's Leuven-Ghent deep-tech axis—combining imec bio-chips and silicon photonics with VIB single-cell diagnostics.

hubs.name: National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS-TIFR)
hubs.summary: Part of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research on Bengaluru's lush GKVK campus—India's premier hub for cellular organization, quantitative biophysics, neurobiology, chemical ecology, and tropical biodiversity genomics.
hubs.nobel: Founded by Obaid Siddiqi (pioneer of Drosophila neurogenetics); anchors the Bengaluru Life Science Cluster (BLiSC) with inStem and C-CAMP.

stages.highschool: Explore the Archives at NCBS and public Science Gallery Bengaluru exhibitions.

rabbitLinks.reason: Sister center of TIFR Mumbai; hosts the Simons Centre uniting statistical physicists with cell biologists.

hubs.name: Genome Institute of Singapore (A*STAR GIS)
hubs.summary: Flagship genomics hub at Singapore's Biopolis leading Asia's largest multi-ethnic population sequencing program (SG100K), spatial omics, RNA biology, and AI-assisted clinical precision medicine.
hubs.nobel: Bridges the global genomic diversity gap by sequencing 100,000+ Southeast, South, and East Asian genomes with longitudinal clinical data.

hubs.name: Africa Health Research Institute (AHRI) & KRISP
hubs.summary: Unites Wellcome-funded AHRI with KRISP (KwaZulu-Natal Research Innovation and Sequencing Platform) in Durban—world-famous for real-time viral genomic surveillance (identifying Beta and Omicron variants), HIV cure immunology, and tuberculosis research.
hubs.nobel: Honored globally (Time100, Nature's 10) for transparent open-data pathogen genomics that alerted the world to SARS-CoV-2 variants in real time.

stages.prof: Global leadership in epidemic genomics, climate-sensitive infectious disease, and equitable biotech.

rabbitLinks.reason: Pairs South African real-time genomic surveillance with AIMS mathematical modeling of infectious outbreaks.

hubs.name: Weizmann Institute Life Sciences & Biochemistry
hubs.summary: Multidisciplinary life-science powerhouse on the Weizmann campus—where Ada Yonath solved the atomic structure of the ribosome, and modern labs lead synthetic stem-cell embryology, bacterial immune defense systems, and personalized nutrition.
hubs.nobel: Ada Yonath won the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for mapping the ribosome's atomic structure via cryo-bio-crystallography.

stages.postdoc: Dean's and Koshland Postdoctoral Fellowships across structural biology and immunology.
stages.assoc_prof: Principal Investigator tracks renowned for rapid lab launch and minimal bureaucracy.
stages.prof: Global leadership in phage-defense biology, synthetic embryo models, and AI-guided medicine.
